findings.issue_text: pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/logger_middleware.go:52 — The "Plugin Request Completed" log line no longer includes a "traceID" field (previously set via tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false)); the replacement ContextualLoggerMiddleware.instrumentContext (contextual_logger_middleware.go) restores pluginId/endpoint/dsName/dsUID/uname via WithContextualAttributes but never re-adds traceID, so downstream log-based alerts/dashboards correlating plugin request logs to traces by "traceID" will silently stop receiving that field

pkg/plugins/log/ifaces.go:5 — Adding FromContext(ctx context.Context) Logger as a new required method on the exported plugins/log.Logger interface is a breaking change for any implementer of this interface outside this diff (e.g. downstream/enterprise or vendored consumers); only two in-repo implementers (TestLogger in fake.go, grafanaInfraLogWrapper in logger.go) were updated, so any other implementation not visible in this partial checkout would fail to compile

pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/metrics_middleware_test.go:15 — Test function is still named TestInstrumentationMiddleware despite the type under test being renamed to MetricsMiddleware, leaving a stale name that no longer matches the code it tests

pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/metrics_middleware.go:186 — In QueryData, if instrumentPluginRequestSize returns plugins.ErrPluginNotRegistered (e.g. a transient registry lookup miss/race at startup), the method returns (nil, err) immediately without ever calling m.next(...), so the real QueryData call to the plugin never executes -- a metrics-instrumentation failure takes down actual plugin functionality instead of just skipping metrics

pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/contextual_logger_middleware.go:59 — SubscribeStream/PublishStream/RunStream pass through without calling instrumentContext, so contextual log fields (pluginId, endpoint, dsUID, uname) are never attached for streaming requests, leaving stream-related log lines without plugin/datasource context and hurting incident diagnosis for stream endpoints

pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/logger_middleware.go:76 — The explicit traceID inclusion via tracing.TraceIDFromContext in logRequest's logParams was removed and not replaced by any equivalent attribute added in contextual_logger_middleware.go's instrumentContext, so "Plugin Request Completed" log lines lose direct traceID correlation, weakening trace-to-log correlation during production incident triage

pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/contextual_logger_middleware.go:27 — instrumentContext, which builds the endpoint/pluginId/dsName/dsUID/uname attrs and attaches them via log.WithContextualAttributes, has zero test coverage — no contextual_logger_middleware_test.go was added despite this being new, behavior-defining logic.

pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/logger_middleware.go:58 — LoggerMiddleware now depends entirely on m.logger.FromContext(ctx) to obtain pluginId/endpoint/dsName/dsUID/uname (previously logged directly from pluginCtx/endpoint), but no logger_middleware_test.go exists in the package, so this fundamental behavioral change (and the coupling to ContextualLoggerMiddleware running upstream) is completely unverified.

pkg/plugins/log/fake.go:46 — TestLogger.FromContext always returns a brand-new NewTestLogger() disconnected from the receiver, so any future test that calls logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...) and then asserts on the original TestLogger's InfoLogs/ErrorLogs will silently see empty/zero results — a false-negative trap that could make broken logging code pass tests.

pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/metrics_middleware_test.go:21 — TestInstrumentationMiddleware only exercises the path where the plugin is present in pluginsRegistry; it never covers m.pluginTarget failing (plugin not found in registry) for QueryData/CallResource/CheckHealth/CollectMetrics, so the behavior-changing edge case where m.next is never called on registry lookup failure is untested.

pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/contextual_logger_middleware.go:59 — SubscribeStream/PublishStream/RunStream on ContextualLoggerMiddleware intentionally skip instrumentContext (unlike QueryData/CallResource/CheckHealth/CollectMetrics), but this asymmetry is undocumented and untested, so a future refactor could silently change this without any test catching it.

goldens.comment: The ContextualLoggerMiddleware methods (QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth, CollectMetrics) panic when a nil request is received. This occurs because they directly access req.PluginContext (via the instrumentContext function) without first checking if req is nil. This is a regression, as previous middleware layers gracefully handled nil requests.

The traceID is no longer logged for plugin requests. During a refactoring, the tracing import and the logic to extract and add traceID from the context to log parameters were removed from the LoggerMiddleware. The newly introduced ContextualLoggerMiddleware does not add this information, resulting in missing traceID in plugin request logs and impacting debugging and request tracing capabilities.

The `TestLogger.FromContext` method returns a new `TestLogger` instance via `NewTestLogger()` instead of returning the receiver (f). This causes logs to be recorded on an un-referenced instance, leading to broken test assertions that expect logs to be recorded on the original logger.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/plugins/log/ifaces.go:5 — Adding FromContext(ctx context.Context) Logger as a new required method on the exported plugins/log.Logger interface is a breaking change for any implementer of this interface outside this diff (e.g. downstream/enterprise or vendored consumers); only two in-repo implementers (TestLogger in fake.go, grafanaInfraLogWrapper in logger.go) were updated, so any other implementation not visible in this partial checkout would fail to compile

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new required method `FromContext(ctx context.Context) Logger` to the exported `pkg/plugins/log.Logger` interface (pkg/plugins/log/ifaces.go). Adding a method to an interface is a compile-time breaking API change for any external (or in-repo, not shown) type that previously implemented `Logger` but is not updated to include this method. The diff only updates two visible implementations (`TestLogger` in fake.go and `grafanaInfraLogWrapper` in logger.go), so the concern about other implementers failing to compile is valid as an API-compatibility issue, though not a runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/pluginsintegration/pluginsintegration.go:156 — The PR is titled as a pure "rename instrumentation middleware to metrics middleware" chore, but CreateMiddlewares now inserts a new NewContextualLoggerMiddleware() into the exported middleware chain and the logger_middleware.go log line drops several previously-logged fields, meaning the change is a behavior/contract change to plugin-request observability rather than a no-op rename as described

adjudication.rationale: The diff is not a pure rename: `CreateMiddlewares` adds a new exported middleware `clientmiddleware.NewContextualLoggerMiddleware()` to the chain (pluginsintegration.go:156), and `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest` removes previously logged fields (`pluginId`, `endpoint`, `uname`, `traceID`, `dsName`, `dsUID`) from `logParams` (logger_middleware.go), switching to `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`. While some of those fields are reintroduced via context in the new middleware’s `instrumentContext` (contextual_logger_middleware.go), `traceID` logging is clearly dropped in this diff and the observability behavior/contract changes compared to before. This is a scope/behavior change concern rather than a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/metrics_middleware_test.go:15 — Test function is still named TestInstrumentationMiddleware despite the type under test being renamed to MetricsMiddleware, leaving a stale name that no longer matches the code it tests

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show the test function remains `func TestInstrumentationMiddleware(t *testing.T)` in the renamed `metrics_middleware_test.go`, but this is only a stale/less-descriptive test name. It does not break compilation or test behavior, so it is a naming/style nit rather than a verifiable defect or important non-bug issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/metrics_middleware.go:186 — In QueryData, if instrumentPluginRequestSize returns plugins.ErrPluginNotRegistered (e.g. a transient registry lookup miss/race at startup), the method returns (nil, err) immediately without ever calling m.next(...), so the real QueryData call to the plugin never executes -- a metrics-instrumentation failure takes down actual plugin functionality instead of just skipping metrics

adjudication.rationale: The metrics middleware treats metrics instrumentation errors as hard failures: e.g., in `CallResource`, it does `if err := m.instrumentPluginRequestSize(...); err != nil { return err }`, which prevents `m.next.CallResource(...)` from executing. `instrumentPluginRequestSize` can return `plugins.ErrPluginNotRegistered` via `pluginTarget` when the registry lookup misses. Although the diff excerpt doesn’t show the full `QueryData` body, the same pattern is strongly implied (and existed in the renamed file), meaning a metrics-only failure can block the actual plugin request.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/metrics_middleware.go:194 — Same as QueryData: CallResource returns early on instrumentPluginRequestSize's ErrPluginNotRegistered without invoking m.next(...), so CallResource requests fail entirely instead of degrading gracefully when the plugin registry lookup misses

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows CallResource (and QueryData) return immediately if `instrumentPluginRequestSize` fails: `if err := m.instrumentPluginRequestSize(...); err != nil { return err }`, and `pluginTarget` can return `plugins.ErrPluginNotRegistered` when the registry lookup misses. This means the middleware can block the downstream `m.next.CallResource(...)` call on a registry miss. However, the diff alone doesn’t establish that this is definitively incorrect vs. an intentional failure mode when a plugin isn’t registered; it’s a design/robustness concern rather than a clearly verifiable defect from the PR context.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/plugins/log/logger.go:48 — FromContext silently falls back to d.New() (dropping ctx's contextual attributes) when the type assertion to *log.ConcreteLogger fails, with no error/warning logged, so pluginId/endpoint/dsUID/uname fields can silently disappear from production logs in some code path with no signal that this happened

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/plugins/log/logger.go, grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext(ctx) does `d.l.FromContext(ctx).(*log.ConcreteLogger)` and, if the assertion fails, returns `d.New()` with no logging or error. That fallback path indeed ignores the provided context.Context and therefore would not carry over any contextual attributes stored in ctx (e.g., those added via log.WithContextualAttributes in the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware). The diff does not prove the assertion can fail in production, but the silent drop is a real, diff-grounded edge-case/observability concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/contextual_logger_middleware.go:59 — SubscribeStream/PublishStream/RunStream pass through without calling instrumentContext, so contextual log fields (pluginId, endpoint, dsUID, uname) are never attached for streaming requests, leaving stream-related log lines without plugin/datasource context and hurting incident diagnosis for stream endpoints

adjudication.rationale: In the new `ContextualLoggerMiddleware`, `instrumentContext` is applied only in `QueryData`, `CallResource`, `CheckHealth`, and `CollectMetrics`, while `SubscribeStream`, `PublishStream`, and `RunStream` simply delegate to `m.next` without enriching the context. This is verifiable in `contextual_logger_middleware.go` (streaming methods lack `ctx = instrumentContext(...)`). That omission means streaming calls will not get the contextual attributes this middleware is intended to add. Whether this is a functional bug depends on whether anything logs using those context attributes for streaming paths (not shown in the diff), but it is a concrete, diff-grounded incompleteness affecting observability.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/logger_middleware.go:76 — The explicit traceID inclusion via tracing.TraceIDFromContext in logRequest's logParams was removed and not replaced by any equivalent attribute added in contextual_logger_middleware.go's instrumentContext, so "Plugin Request Completed" log lines lose direct traceID correlation, weakening trace-to-log correlation during production incident triage

adjudication.rationale: In logger_middleware.go, the explicit `traceID := tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false)` block that appended `"traceID"` into `logParams` was removed. The new approach logs via `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`, relying on context-enriched attributes. However, the new `contextual_logger_middleware.go` `instrumentContext` only adds `endpoint`, `pluginId`, optional `dsName/dsUID`, and `uname` via `log.WithContextualAttributes(ctx, p)` and does not add any trace identifier. From the diff alone, there is no equivalent traceID attribute being added alongside the new contextual logger enrichment, implying a likely observability regression rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/contextual_logger_middleware.go:27 — instrumentContext, which builds the endpoint/pluginId/dsName/dsUID/uname attrs and attaches them via log.WithContextualAttributes, has zero test coverage — no contextual_logger_middleware_test.go was added despite this being new, behavior-defining logic.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new behavior-defining logic in the new file `pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/contextual_logger_middleware.go`, including `instrumentContext(...)` which constructs attributes (endpoint, pluginId, dsName/dsUID, uname) and attaches them via `log.WithContextualAttributes`, and the middleware methods that call it. The diff does not add any corresponding test file (e.g., no `contextual_logger_middleware_test.go` is present), and the only test change shown is renaming `instrumentation_middleware_test.go` to `metrics_middleware_test.go`. This is a concrete, diff-grounded gap in test coverage for newly introduced middleware behavior, but not a functional defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/logger_middleware.go:58 — LoggerMiddleware now depends entirely on m.logger.FromContext(ctx) to obtain pluginId/endpoint/dsName/dsUID/uname (previously logged directly from pluginCtx/endpoint), but no logger_middleware_test.go exists in the package, so this fundamental behavioral change (and the coupling to ContextualLoggerMiddleware running upstream) is completely unverified.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a nontrivial behavior/architecture change in `LoggerMiddleware`: `logRequest` no longer appends `pluginId`, `endpoint`, `dsName`, `dsUID`, or `uname` from `pluginCtx`/`endpoint` and instead logs via `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)` (see `logger_middleware.go` change from `m.logger.Info(...)` to `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)` and removal of those fields from `logParams`). The only place those attributes are now added is the newly introduced `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` (`instrumentContext` uses `log.WithContextualAttributes(ctx, ...)`) and it is placed before `NewLoggerMiddleware(...)` in `CreateMiddlewares`, creating an implicit ordering/coupling. The diff does not add/update any tests for `LoggerMiddleware` to verify this new dependency or that the expected fields still appear in logs when the middleware stack is configured correctly. The claim that *no* `logger_middleware_test.go` exists cannot be proven from the diff alone, but the lack of any added/modified tests for this behavior change is diff-grounded.

adjudication.rationale: In the renamed `metrics_middleware_test.go`, `TestInstrumentationMiddleware` still sets up the plugins registry with the plugin present (see the diff where it uses `newMetricsMiddleware(promRegistry, pluginsRegistry)` after registering the plugin). In `metrics_middleware.go`, both `instrumentPluginRequestSize` and `instrumentPluginRequest` call `m.pluginTarget(...)`, which returns `plugins.ErrPluginNotRegistered` when the plugin is not found and exits early before calling `m.next.*`. That error path (registry lookup failure causing early return / `m.next` not being called) is not exercised by the shown test setup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/contextual_logger_middleware.go:59 — SubscribeStream/PublishStream/RunStream on ContextualLoggerMiddleware intentionally skip instrumentContext (unlike QueryData/CallResource/CheckHealth/CollectMetrics), but this asymmetry is undocumented and untested, so a future refactor could silently change this without any test catching it.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/contextual_logger_middleware.go, QueryData/CallResource/CheckHealth/CollectMetrics all wrap ctx via instrumentContext(...), but SubscribeStream/PublishStream/RunStream simply delegate to m.next without calling instrumentContext. The diff includes no comment explaining why streaming endpoints are excluded and there are no tests in this diff covering that behavior, so the asymmetry could be accidentally changed in future refactors without detection.
